# 5.4 Square-root decomposition

Phase 5 (Range data structures), target rating 1800–2100. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Blocks of size √n (`blocks`)

Split the array into blocks of about √n with a summary per block; updates touch one block, queries touch O(√n) blocks and items.

**Works because:** A block's summary can be rebuilt in O(√n) and queried in O(1).

### Rebuild every sqrt(q) changes (`rebuild-batches`)

The structure is rebuilt once per batch of about sqrt(q) changes, and a question looks at the table of the last rebuild together with the few changes made since.

**Works because:** A rebuild costs about O(n), a question can combine the table with one change at a time (a minimum, a count), and changes are only added, never taken back.

### Small versus large parameter (`threshold-split`)

Handle small parameters (below √n) with a table and large ones directly, because there are few large ones or each has few steps.

**Works because:** Work for a parameter k is about n / k when large and fits in an O(n·√n) table when small.

### Looks like a block problem, but a Fenwick sweep is enough (`no-blocks`)

Offline questions about ranges or sets of points that tempt a split into blocks, but a sort by one end and a Fenwick tree over the other end answers them in O((n + q) log n).

**Works because:** All questions are known first, and each answer is a sum of prefix counts.
